mainTopic: Carrying through a סטיו (מקום פטור), and the ברייתא of the four domains of שבת
overview: The גמרא first looks for a precedent for the view that a person who carries from a shop to the plaza through a סטיו is חייב, even though the סטיו is a מקום פטור lying in the middle. Two comparisons are rejected: walking through רשות הרבים, and carrying exactly four אמות. In both, the middle area is only exempt for this carrier, not by its nature. A third comparison works: carrying through צדי רשות הרבים. רב פפא challenges it from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. רב אחא בריה דרב איקא answers that where there are stakes, even רבי אליעזר בן יעקב agrees the sides are exempt. רבי יוחנן then adds that בן עזאי, who exempts the walker, agrees that a thrower is חייב, and a ברייתא confirms this. Next, the גמרא quotes a ברייתא listing the four domains of שבת: רשות היחיד, רשות הרבים, כרמלית, and מקום פטור. It defines each one, along with shared courtyards that need an עירוב and the threshold case. Finally, the גמרא asks what the words "זו היא רשות היחיד" exclude, and begins quoting רבי יהודה's view, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First precedent: walking with an object in the public domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא compares the סטיו case to a person who carries an object while walking through רשות הרבים. While he walks he is not yet liable, but when he puts it down he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just like a person who carries an object through the public domain. There, even though he is exempt the whole time he is holding it and walking, when he puts it down he is liable. Here too it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a comparison to show that an exempt stretch in the middle does not prevent liability. Someone walking through רשות הרבים with an object is not liable during the walk, yet he becomes liable once he puts it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case being explained has a 'פטור zone' (the סטיו) between the shop and the plaza. The גמרא points out that a walker in רשות הרבים also passes through a long stretch where he is not yet liable, and he is still חייב at the end. So, the argument goes, an exempt middle is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like; a formula that introduces a comparison or precedent
One who carries or transfers an object
The public domain
Exempt / liable
He puts it down (the הנחה, setting it down)

steps.confusionAlert: Walking with the object is not 'allowed'. The גמרא only means he has not yet become liable for a חטאת, because the מלאכה is completed only when he puts the object down.

phrases.aramaic: מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַמַּעֲבִיר חֵפֶץ בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים.
phrases.english: It is just like one who carries an object through the public domain.
There, is it not so that even though
as long as he holds it and walks he is exempt,
when he puts it down he is liable?
Here too it is no different.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַמַּעֲבִיר חֵפֶץ בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the implied question from the previous section of the daf: how can someone be חייב when a מקום פטור lies between the start and the end of his carrying?
steps.raayaObject: Liability can exist even when the object passes through an exempt stretch before being put down.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of a person walking through רשות הרבים with an object: he is פטור while walking and חייב once he puts it down.

steps.title: Rejection: in the public domain every spot is potentially liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. In רשות הרבים, wherever he puts the object down is a place of liability. The סטיו is a true מקום פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that comparable?! There, anywhere he puts it down is a place of liability. Here, if he puts it down in the colonnade, it is an exempt place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and says the walking case is not similar. It shows exactly why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While walking in רשות הרבים, the middle area is not really 'exempt'. If he put the object down anywhere there, he would be חייב. The סטיו is different: putting the object down there creates no liability at all. So the walker never actually passes through a true exempt zone.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it comparable?! Rejects an analogy
A place where putting down creates liability
An exempt area; putting down there creates no liability
A colonnade or covered walkway, treated here as a מקום פטור

phrases.english: Is that comparable?!
There, anywhere that he puts it down
is a place of liability.
Here, if he puts it down in the colonnade,
it is an exempt place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the precedent brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The analogy between walking in רשות הרבים and passing through the סטיו
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In רשות הרבים the middle area is potentially liable everywhere. The סטיו is truly exempt, so the two cases are not parallel.

steps.title: Second precedent: carrying exactly four cubits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a better comparison. Someone moves an object in רשות הרבים from the start of four אמות to the end of four אמות. Inside the four אמות he would be פטור, yet at the end he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is just like one who carries an object from the beginning of four cubits to the end of four cubits. There, even though if he put it down within the four cubits he would be exempt, when he puts it down at the end of the four cubits he is liable. Here too it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: After the first comparison fails, the גמרא offers a new precedent. Here the middle area really is a place where putting down creates no liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying in רשות הרבים is only חייב after moving the object four אמות. So the space inside the first four אמות is a zone where putting it down makes him פטור. Even so, he is חייב when he reaches the end. This seems to fix the flaw from step 2, because now there truly is a 'פטור zone' in the middle.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a replacement answer after the previous one failed
Four cubits, the minimum distance for liability when carrying in רשות הרבים
From the beginning of four cubits to the end of four cubits

phrases.english: Rather, it is just like one who carries an object
from the beginning of four cubits to the end of four cubits.
There, is it not so that even though

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי מַנַּח לֵיהּ בְּתוֹךְ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: if he put it down within four cubits he would be exempt,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מַנַּח לֵיהּ בְּסוֹף אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: when he puts it down at the end of four cubits he is liable?
Here too it is no different.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַמַּעֲבִיר חֵפֶץ מִתְּחִלַּת אַרְבַּע לְסוֹף אַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected precedent of step 1 with one designed to answer the objection in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: Liability can exist even when the object passes through an area where putting it down would be פטור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Carrying exactly four אמות in רשות הרבים: putting it down inside the four אמות is פטור, but putting it down at the end is חייב.

steps.title: Rejection: exempt only for this person versus exempt for everyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the second comparison too. The area inside four אמות is exempt only for this particular carrier, while for the rest of the world it is a place of liability. The סטיו is exempt for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that comparable?! There, for this man it is an exempt place, but for the whole world it is a place of liability. Here, for the whole world it is an exempt place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the four-אמות comparison as well. It explains that the 'exempt' area there is a different kind of exemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside the four אמות, the spot is still רשות הרבים. It is exempt only because this person has not yet carried far enough. Someone who started further away would be חייב putting an object down there. The סטיו is exempt because of what the place itself is, no matter who carries there, so the precedent does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: With regard to this particular man
For the whole world, for anyone

steps.whatToRemember: Both precedents fail for the same basic reason. In them, the 'exempt' middle exists only because the מלאכה is not yet complete, or only for this particular carrier. The סטיו is a מקום פטור by its very nature, for everyone. The search for a real precedent continues.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out an important distinction in הלכות שבת. One kind of פטור comes from the person's action being incomplete. Another kind comes from the status of the place itself. A precedent for the סטיו case must involve the second kind.

phrases.english: Is that comparable?!

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, לְגַבֵּי דְּהַאי גַּבְרָא מְקוֹם פְּטוּר הוּא,
phrases.english: There, with regard to this man it is an exempt place,
but for the whole world it is a place of liability.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא לְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מְקוֹם פְּטוּר הוּא.
phrases.english: Here, for the whole world it is an exempt place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second precedent brought in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The analogy between the four-אמות case and passing through the סטיו
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The area inside four אמות is exempt only relative to this carrier and is a מקום חיוב for others. The סטיו is a מקום פטור absolutely, for everyone.

steps.title: A third comparison: carrying along the sides of the public street
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא compares the סטיו case to carrying from a private domain to a public domain by way of צדי רשות הרבים. Putting the object down on the sides is exempt, yet putting it down in the street itself makes him חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is just like a person who carries from a private domain to a public domain by passing along the sides of the public domain. In that case, even though he would be exempt if he put the object down on the sides, he is liable when he puts it down in the public domain itself. Here too, it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third precedent to show that passing through an exempt area on the way does not cancel liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier comparisons failed because the 'exempt' area was not exempt for everyone. The sides of the street, where the crowds do not walk, are a place that is exempt for everyone, just like the סטיו. Even so, carrying through them into the real street still makes a person חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: The sides of the public domain: narrow strips along the houses where crowds do not walk
It is no different

phrases.english: Rather, it is just like
one who carries out from a private domain to a public domain
by way of the sides of the public domain.
There, is it not so that even though

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי מַנַּח לֵיהּ אַצִּדֵּי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים — פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: if he places it on the sides of the public domain he is exempt,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מַנַּח לֵיהּ בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים — חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: yet when he places it in the public domain he is liable?
Here too, it is no different.
phrases.notes: Applying the precedent to the סטיו case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַמּוֹצִיא מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the comparison rejected in step 4 with one where the exempt area is exempt for everyone.
steps.raayaObject: That carrying through a true מקום פטור (the סטיו) into רשות הרבים still makes a person חייב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of carrying through צדי רשות הרבים, which are exempt for everyone, where putting the object down in the street makes him חייב.

steps.title: רב פפא objects: one תנא treats the sides as full public domain
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the comparison only works for the רבנן, who hold that צדי רשות הרבים are not like רשות הרבים. According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who says they are like רשות הרבים, the sides are not exempt, so the precedent fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objected: This works well for the רבנן, who say that the sides of the public domain are not like the public domain. But according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who said that the sides of the public domain are like the public domain, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks the new comparison. He points out that according to one תנא, the sides of the street are not an exempt area at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof needs the sides to be a true exempt area, like the סטיו. For רבי אליעזר בן יעקב the sides count as real רשות הרבים. Then the case is just carrying from one domain to another, and it proves nothing about passing through an exempt area.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected to it
It works well for, or it is fine according to
It is considered like the public domain
What is there to say? (a challenge formula)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa strongly objected to it:
This works well for the Rabbis, who say

phrases.aramaic: צִדֵּי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים לָאו כִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: that the sides of the public domain are not like the public domain.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב דְּאָמַר
phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov, who said

phrases.aramaic: צִדֵּי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים כִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: that the sides of the public domain are like the public domain,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the precedent brought in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of the סטיו to צדי רשות הרבים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the sides are real רשות הרבים, not an exempt area. So the precedent does not show liability after passing through a מקום פטור.

steps.title: רב אחא answers: with stakes in place, the sides are exempt for everyone
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא answers that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב only called the sides רשות הרבים when there are no stakes (חיפופי). When stakes block the strip, even he would agree it is not רשות הרבים. So the precedent matches the סטיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא said to him: Granted, you heard that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב said the sides of the public domain are like the public domain where there are no stakes. But where there are stakes, did you hear him say that? Therefore, the case is similar to this one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא defends the comparison by limiting the opinion of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב to sides that have no stakes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stakes along the wall keep the crowds from walking on the strip. Without stakes, people sometimes walk there, so רבי אליעזר בן יעקב counts it as public. With stakes, nobody walks there, so it is a true exempt area according to everyone, and the precedent works for all opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted that you heard (introduces a limit on a cited opinion)
Stakes placed along walls that keep the public away
Therefore
It is similar to this case

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Ika, said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵימוֹר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
phrases.english: Granted that you heard Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר צִדֵּי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים כִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים דָּמֵי
phrases.english: say that the sides of the public domain are like the public domain
where there are no stakes.
But where there are stakes,
did you hear him say that?
Therefore, it is similar to this case.
phrases.notes: Similar to the סטיו, so it serves as a precedent.

steps.whatToRemember: The final precedent for the סטיו is carrying through צדי רשות הרבים that have stakes. That area is exempt for everyone, yet putting the object down in the street afterward still makes him חייב.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא אֵימוֹר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's objection from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the opinion of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב applies only where there are no stakes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב treats all side strips as רשות הרבים, which would ruin the precedent.
steps.terutzMaskana: With stakes in place, everyone agrees the sides are an exempt area. So the precedent stands.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: בן עזאי agrees that throwing is liable
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that בן עזאי, who exempts a person who walks through the סטיו carrying an object, agrees that throwing an object through the סטיו makes a person חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: And בן עזאי agrees in the case of one who throws.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the opinion of בן עזאי and limits how far his exemption goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עזאי's reason for exempting the walker is that walking counts as stopping (מהלך כעומד), so the object 'rests' in the סטיו. A thrown object never stops in the סטיו. So even בן עזאי agrees that throwing is like moving the object directly from one domain to the other.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees
A תנא who holds that walking counts as stopping
One who throws

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
And Ben Azzai agrees in the case of one who throws.
phrases.notes: He agrees that the thrower is liable.

steps.confusionAlert: בן עזאי does not argue about every way of moving the object through the סטיו. He exempts only walking and carrying, because walking counts as stopping. Throwing has no such stop.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וּמוֹדֶה בֶּן עַזַּאי בְּזוֹרֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending the רבנן to defining the limits of בן עזאי's exemption.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even בן עזאי holds that someone who throws an object through a סטיו is חייב.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that carrying from a store to a plaza through a סטיו makes a person חייב in all four ways of moving an object. בן עזאי exempts only carrying out and carrying in, and agrees that handing and throwing make a person חייב, just as רבי יוחנן said.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: One who carries out from a store to a plaza by way of a colonnade is liable. This applies equally to one who carries out, one who carries in, one who throws, and one who hands over. בן עזאי says: One who carries out or carries in is exempt, but one who hands over or throws is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן's statement about בן עזאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion (the תנא קמא) holds a person חייב in all four ways of moving the object. בן עזאי splits them: walking out or walking in is exempt, because the walker counts as stopping in the סטיו. Handing and throwing are one continuous motion, so even he holds them חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא (a supporting source)
Store (a private domain)
Plaza (a public domain)
Colonnade, a covered walkway that serves as an exempt area
One who hands over or extends an object by hand
One who carries in

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, moving an object through a סטיו makes a person חייב in every way. בן עזאי exempts only walking (carrying out or carrying in), and agrees that handing and throwing are חייב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that בן עזאי's whole exemption rests on the idea that walking counts as stopping. Wherever there is no walking, his exemption does not apply.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
One who carries out from a store to a plaza
by way of a colonnade is liable.
This is the same for one who carries out and one who carries in,
one who throws and one who hands over.
Ben Azzai says:
One who carries out or carries in is exempt,
phrases.notes: Because walking counts as stopping inside the סטיו.

phrases.english: one who hands over or throws is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's statement in step 8 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that בן עזאי agrees a thrower is חייב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא, where בן עזאי explicitly rules that one who hands over or throws is חייב.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists four domains for שבת
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that there are four domains for the laws of שבת: רשות היחיד, רשות הרבים, כרמלית, and מקום פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: There are four domains for שבת: a private domain, a public domain, a כרמלית, and an exempt place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting a ברייתא that lists the four kinds of domains for carrying on שבת. This sets up the definitions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the סוגיא dealt with specific cases like the סטיו. Now the גמרא steps back to give the full map of domains. There are two Torah-level domains (רשות היחיד, רשות הרבים) and two others, the כרמלית and the מקום פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Rabbis taught": introduces a ברייתא
Domains or areas, for the laws of carrying
An in-between domain that the Rabbis treat strictly
An exempt place, which is not treated as any domain

steps.whyThisMatters: This four-part map is the foundation for all the laws of carrying on שבת throughout מסכת שבת.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There are four domains for Shabbat:
the private domain, and the public domain,
and karmelit, and an exempt place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section. It moves from the specific סטיו discussion to a general ברייתא about all the domains.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are four domains for שבת: רשות היחיד, רשות הרבים, כרמלית, and מקום פטור.

steps.title: Defining a full private domain
steps.stepSummary: A full רשות היחיד is a ditch ten טפחים deep and four wide, or a fence (a raised area) ten טפחים high and four wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a private domain? A ditch that is ten טפחים deep and four wide, and likewise a raised fence that is ten high and four wide. That is a full private domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains the first domain on its list, the רשות היחיד. It gives its exact size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things make a רשות היחיד: an area of at least four by four טפחים, and a height difference of ten טפחים from its surroundings. The ditch goes ten down. The raised "fence" goes ten up. Either one works.

keyTerms.meaning: A ditch or trench
A fence or wall, here a raised area
Ten טפחים (handbreadths)
Full or complete, a true Torah-level domain

phrases.english: And what is the private domain?
A ditch that is ten handbreadths deep
and four handbreadths wide,
and likewise a fence that is ten high
and four wide
this is a full-fledged private domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the first domain listed in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A full רשות היחיד is an area at least four by four טפחים with a ten-טפח height difference, such as a deep ditch or a high raised area.

steps.title: Defining a full public domain
steps.stepSummary: A full רשות הרבים is a main road, a large plaza, or alleyways that are open at both ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a public domain? A main road, a large plaza, and alleyways open at both ends. That is a full public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains the second domain, the רשות הרבים, by giving examples of places where crowds pass through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A רשות הרבים is defined by public traffic: wide roads and plazas where many people walk. An alley counts only if it is open at both ends, so people use it as a through-path. An alley that is closed at one end does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: A main road or highway
A large city plaza
Alleyways open at both ends, used as through-paths

phrases.english: And what is the public domain?
A main road and a large plaza,
and alleyways open at both ends
this is a full-fledged public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the second domain listed in step 10, parallel to the definition of רשות היחיד in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A full רשות הרבים is a main road, a large plaza, or an alley open at both ends.

steps.title: The punishment for carrying between the two full domains
steps.stepSummary: Carrying between a full רשות היחיד and a full רשות הרבים is forbidden by the Torah. Doing it by mistake requires a חטאת. Doing it on purpose brings כרת or סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not carry out from this private domain to this public domain, and one may not carry in from this public domain to this private domain. If he carried out or in by mistake, he must bring a חטאת. If he did it on purpose, he is punished with כרת, and with stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that both full domains are defined, the ברייתא states the law: moving an object between them is a full Torah violation of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "זו" ("this") stresses that the full punishment applies only to these exact full domains just defined. The punishment depends on the case: a mistake requires a חטאת. Doing it on purpose without warning and witnesses brings כרת. Doing it with warning and witnesses brings סקילה by בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying out, from private to public
Carrying in, from public to private
By mistake, unintentionally
On purpose, intentionally
Spiritual cutting off, a heavenly punishment
Stoned, a בית דין punishment

phrases.english: One may not carry out from this private domain
to this public domain,
and one may not carry in from this public domain
to this private domain,
and if he carried out or carried in unwittingly
he is liable to bring a sin-offering,
phrases.notes: A חטאת is brought for a mistaken violation of a sin that carries כרת.

phrases.english: intentionally, he is punished with karet, and is stoned.
phrases.notes: כרת applies without warning and witnesses. Stoning applies with warning and witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מוֹצִיאִין מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד זוֹ לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the law to the two domains defined in steps 11 and 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying between a full רשות היחיד and a full רשות הרבים is a Torah violation: a mistake requires a חטאת, and doing it on purpose brings כרת or סקילה.

steps.title: The כרמלית and carrying within it
steps.stepSummary: A sea, a valley, a colonnade, and a כרמלית are neither public nor private domain. One may not carry within them, but if one did, there is no Torah liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a sea, a valley, a colonnade, and a כרמלית are neither like a public domain nor like a private domain. One may not carry and put down an object within it. If he did carry and put it down within it, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא turns to the third domain, the כרמלית. It explains that the כרמלית is a middle category and that carrying four אמות inside it carries no Torah punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These places lack the crowds of a רשות הרבים and lack the walls of a רשות היחיד, so they are neither. The Rabbis forbade carrying four אמות inside them, just like in a רשות הרבים. Because the ban is only rabbinic, a person who does it is פטור from Torah punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: A valley or open field
A colonnade, a roofed walkway with pillars
Carrying and putting down, here moving an object four אמות
Exempt from Torah punishment

phrases.english: But a sea and a valley
and a colonnade and the karmelit
is neither like the public domain
nor like the private domain.
And one may not carry and place an object within it.
phrases.notes: This means carrying it four אמות, as in a רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: And if he carried and placed within it, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 13. Unlike the two full domains, the כרמלית carries only a rabbinic ban.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sea, a valley, and a colonnade are a כרמלית, neither public nor private. Carrying within it is rabbinically forbidden, but there is no Torah liability.

steps.title: Carrying between a כרמלית and the other domains
steps.stepSummary: One may not carry between a כרמלית and either a רשות הרבים or a רשות היחיד, but someone who does is exempt from Torah punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not carry out from it to a public domain, nor from a public domain into it. One may not carry in from a private domain into it, nor from it into a private domain. If he carried out or in, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the כרמלית rules. Moving objects between a כרמלית and either full domain is forbidden, but there is no Torah punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a כרמלית is not a real רשות הרבים or רשות היחיד, moving an object in or out of it never connects two Torah-level domains. So the Rabbis forbade it in every direction, but a person who does it is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: From within it, meaning from the כרמלית
Into it, meaning into the כרמלית

steps.confusionAlert: Here פטור does NOT mean "allowed." The ברייתא clearly says "אין מוציאין", it is forbidden. פטור only means there is no Torah punishment (no חטאת, כרת, or סקילה), because the ban is rabbinic.
steps.whatToRemember: Carrying between full רשות היחיד and full רשות הרבים is a Torah violation (חטאת, כרת, סקילה). Anything involving a כרמלית is forbidden only by the Rabbis, so a person who does it is פטור but still did something wrong.

phrases.english: And one may not carry out from it to the public domain,
nor from the public domain into it.
And one may not bring from the private domain into it,
nor from it into the private domain.
And if he carried out or carried in, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the כרמלית rule from step 14 to carrying between the כרמלית and the other domains.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying between a כרמלית and either a רשות הרבים or a רשות היחיד is rabbinically forbidden, with no Torah liability.

steps.title: Shared courtyards and closed alleyways need an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: Courtyards shared by many people, and alleyways that are not open at both ends, are permitted for carrying only if the residents made an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Courtyards that belong to many people, and alleyways that are not open at both ends: if they made an עירוב, carrying is permitted. If they did not make an עירוב, carrying is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list of domains. It now describes places that are truly private by Torah law, but where חז"ל still restricted carrying unless an עירוב is made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, these courtyards and closed alleyways are a full רשות היחיד, because they are enclosed. But many families share them, so חז"ל forbade carrying between the houses and the shared area. An עירוב joins all the residents into one 'household,' and that removes the rabbinic ban.

keyTerms.meaning: Courtyards shared by many households
Alleyways onto which several courtyards open
They made an עירוב (a joining of the residents into one unit)
Permitted / forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse these with the open alleyways of step 12. Alleyways open at both ends are part of רשות הרבים. Alleyways that are NOT open at both ends are enclosed and private, and the only problem with them is rabbinic.

phrases.english: Courtyards belonging to many people
and alleyways that are not open at both ends,
phrases.notes: Contrast with the open-ended alleyways of רשות הרבים in step 12.

phrases.english: if they made an eruv, they are permitted.
If they did not make an eruv, they are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲצֵרוֹת שֶׁל רַבִּים וּמְבוֹאוֹת שֶׁאֵינָן מְפוּלָּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list of domains, adding enclosed shared areas that are restricted only by rabbinic law.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shared courtyards and closed alleyways are permitted for carrying only with an עירוב.

steps.title: A person standing on the threshold
steps.stepSummary: A person standing on a threshold that is a מקום פטור may take from and give to the homeowner inside, or the poor man outside. He may not pass objects from one to the other, but if he does, all three are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person standing on the threshold may take from the homeowner and give to him, and may take from the poor man and give to him. But he may not take from the homeowner and give to the poor man, or take from the poor man and give to the homeowner. And if he did take and give, all three of them are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a practical example of a מקום פטור, an exempt area. Here the exempt area is a threshold that sits between the house and the street.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מקום פטור belongs to neither domain. So moving things between it and either side breaks no rule at all. Passing an object from the house to the street through the threshold is forbidden by חז"ל, because it looks like carrying from domain to domain. Still, there is no Torah violation, because the object stopped in an exempt place along the way.

keyTerms.meaning: A threshold or doorstep
The homeowner, standing inside, in רשות היחיד
A poor man, standing outside, in רשות הרבים
An exempt area, belonging to neither domain (the idea behind this case)
All three are exempt

steps.confusionAlert: The word "exempt" (פטורים) does not mean it was allowed from the start. The ברייתא first says he should not do it (ובלבד שלא). "Exempt" only means there is no Torah punishment after the fact.

phrases.english: A person standing on the threshold
may take from the homeowner and give to him,
phrases.notes: The homeowner is inside, in the private domain.

phrases.english: may take from the poor man and give to him,
phrases.notes: The poor man is outside, in the public domain.

phrases.english: as long as he does not take from the homeowner
and give to the poor man,
or take from the poor man and give to the homeowner.
And if he did take and give —
all three of them are exempt.
phrases.notes: The three are the homeowner, the poor man, and the person on the threshold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the fourth domain, the מקום פטור, and illustrates it with the threshold.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Transferring between a מקום פטור and either domain is fully permitted. Passing an object through it from domain to domain is rabbinically forbidden but carries no Torah liability.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule of מקום פטור: an object that stops in an exempt place breaks the Torah's chain of carrying from domain to domain.

steps.title: Others say the threshold can belong to either side
steps.stepSummary: אחרים hold that a threshold takes on the status of the house when the door is open, and of the outside when the door is locked. If it is ten טפחים high and four wide, it is its own domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say: a threshold serves as two domains. When the door is open, it is like the inside. When the door is locked, it is like the outside. And if the threshold is ten טפחים high and four טפחים wide, it is a domain of its own.
steps.whatsHappening: A different תנא, called אחרים, disagrees with the previous ruling about the threshold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the previous step, the threshold was a neutral exempt area. According to אחרים, an ordinary threshold has no independent status. It joins whichever side it practically serves: when the door is open it serves the house, and when the door is locked it serves the street. Only a threshold big enough to be a full רשות היחיד by itself (ten high, four wide) stands on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: "Others": a name used for a certain תנא (often identified with רבי מאיר)
Serves two domains
A locked doorway
A domain unto itself

phrases.english: Others say:
A threshold serves as two domains.
When the door is open, it is like the inside;
when the door is locked, it is like the outside.
And if the threshold was
ten handbreadths high and four handbreadths wide,
phrases.notes: These are the same measurements as a full רשות היחיד in step 11.

phrases.english: it is a domain unto itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: אִיסְקוּפָּה מְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת שְׁתֵּי רְשׁוּיוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a dissenting תנאי view on the status of the threshold from step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ordinary threshold follows the house when the door is open and the street when the door is locked. A threshold ten by four is its own רשות היחיד.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of the four domains ends here: רשות היחיד, רשות הרבים, כרמלית, and מקום פטור. The two views on the threshold are a neutral exempt area (first view) or an extension of whichever side it serves (אחרים).

steps.title: What does "this is a private domain" exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins analyzing the ברייתא. It notes the emphatic phrase "זו היא רשות היחיד" and asks what case it comes to exclude.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: "This is a private domain." What does this come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts discussing the ברייתא it just quoted. This question sets up the next step, where an answer will be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא could simply have listed the measurements of a private domain. Instead it added the emphatic words "this is," which suggest "only this and nothing else." The גמרא assumes these extra words must be ruling out some other case that someone might have considered a רשות היחיד.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Master said": a formula for quoting a source the גמרא is about to analyze
"To exclude what?": asking what an extra word or phrase rules out

phrases.english: The Master said:
"This is a private domain."
What does this come to exclude?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: זוֹ הִיא רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד, לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from quoting the ברייתא to analyzing its wording, returning to the definition of רשות היחיד from step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case the emphatic phrase "זו היא רשות היחיד" is meant to exclude.

steps.title: It excludes the view of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the phrase excludes רבי יהודה's view. It begins quoting a ברייתא about a man who owns two houses on opposite sides of the public domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the view of רבי יהודה. As it was taught: Furthermore, רבי יהודה said: One who has two houses on two sides of the public domain makes... (the quote continues on the next amud).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. It begins bringing a ברייתא that shows which kind of 'private domain' is being ruled out. The quote is cut off and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה will teach that a man with houses on both sides of a public street can mark off that stretch of street and turn it into a private domain. The words "זו היא רשות היחיד" teach that only a true enclosed area, like a ditch or a raised area, counts. A marked-off section of a public road does not.

keyTerms.meaning: "Furthermore": introduces an additional, more far-reaching statement
"As it was taught" (in a ברייתא)
The two sides of the public domain

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence breaks off at "עושה" ("makes"). רבי יהודה's full ruling, and the reason the חכמים reject it, come on the next amud.

phrases.english: To exclude that view of Rabbi Yehuda.
As it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: יֶתֶר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda said:
One who has two houses
on two sides of the public domain
makes...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase "זו היא רשות היחיד" excludes רבי יהודה's view that a section of public domain between two of a person's houses can be made into a private domain.
